regions.text: 偶然と絶對形而上的必然との開係および經驗必然と形而上的偶然との開係に焼て更に詳しく考察して見なければならぬ。

quote.translation: We must next consider more closely the relation between primal contingency and absolute metaphysical necessity, and the relation between empirical necessity and metaphysical contingency.

regions.text: 先っ原始偶然と絶對形而上的必然との開係はどうであるか。

quote.translation: What, first, is the relation between primal contingency and absolute metaphysical necessity?

regions.text: 原始偶然は因果系列の原始起始として假説地平に於て得られた概念である。経驗必然の因果系列を無限に遡るときに理念として原始偶然の概念へ到達したのである。

quote.translation: Primal contingency is a concept obtained on the hypothetical horizon as the primal beginning of the causal series: going back infinitely along the causal series of empirical necessity, we arrived, as at an idea, at the concept of primal contingency.

regions.text: 原始偶然は『原始事件』（Urereignis）であり、『歴史の端初』（AnfangderGe-schichte）である（Sehelling,SammticheWerkeE,2,1857,S153）。

quote.translation: Primal contingency is the "primal event" (Urereignis), the "beginning of history" (Anfang der Geschichte) (Schelling, Sämmtliche Werke II, 2, 1857, S. 153).

regions.text: 然しながら、因果的連鎖に制約された必然的系列の絶對的起始はまた系列の各成員たる經驗的必然のすべてを部分として含蓄する全體と考へることも出來る。

quote.translation: The absolute beginning of the necessary series conditioned by the causal chain can, however, also be thought as the whole that implicitly contains as its parts all the empirical necessities that are the members of the series.

regions.text: 他方にあつて、絶對的形而上約必然とは離接的地平に於て形而上的偶然のすべてを都分とする全體である。さうして全體たる絶對的必然は部分たる離接肢の措定を制約するとも見ることが出来るから、因果系列の絶對起始とも考へ待るものである。

quote.translation: Absolute metaphysical necessity, on the other hand, is the whole that has as its parts all the metaphysical contingencies on the disjunctive horizon, and since absolute necessity as the whole can also be seen as conditioning the positing of the disjuncts as its parts, it can also be thought as the absolute beginning of the causal series.

regions.text: 系列な見方と外延約な見方とが斯やうに互に交換され得る限り原始偶然と絶對形面上的必然とは同一のものでなければならない。

quote.translation: Insofar as the serial view and the extensional view can be exchanged for one another in this way, primal contingency and absolute metaphysical necessity must be one and the same.

regions.text: なほ假說的地平にあつて

quote.translation: We might note, further, that on the hypothetical horizon the infinite causal series was represented in the form of a straight line, with primal contingency thought as its ideal beginning; but true infinity is represented in the form of a circle, in which the last of the series returns to the first, and absolute metaphysical necessity is then thought as the whole circle comprehending each of the circle's parts.
